Alabama.initiatives_raw: Alabama $199.28M Budget Period 2 Funding Initiative Name Initiative Description Collaborative EHR, Information Technology (IT), and Cybersecurity Modernizes healthcare IT infrastructure by establishing regional hubs for IT and cybersecurity support and will assist with EHR integration for rural hospitals and clinics. Reduces overall technology costs and improve interoperability while allowing independent providers to maintain their organizational autonomy. Rural Health Expands access to specialty and emergent care by creating a coordinated network of telehealth hubs. Links first responders, EMS, and local hospitals directly to regional referral centers. Delivers advanced services like remote patient monitoring, tele-stroke, and tele- behavioral health directly into rural communities to reduce unnecessary patient transfers. Maternal and Fetal Health Connects rural facilities with maternal-fetal medicine specialists through advanced digital tools and provides access to telerobotic ultrasound. Addresses critical shortages of local obstetric services to reduce high-risk maternal and infant mortality. Expands an emergency labor and delivery cart pilot program to offer lifesaving stabilization for newborns and mothers pending transfer to a more appropriate hospital setting. Rural Workforce Invests in coordinated training and recruitment pipelines for a broad range of clinical healthcare professionals including but not limited to, physicians, nurses, EMS professionals, certified nurse midwives, dentists, dental hygienists, and dental assistants. Grows the local workforce by leveraging remote learning and strategic clinical partnerships with educational institutions. Provides financialincentives for providers to practice in rural areas while expanding Graduate Medical Education (GME) programs. Cancer Digital Regionalization Replicates the successful, evidence-based model of Alabama's Operation Wipe Out program to target various cancers for early detection. Utilizes decentralized, cross-sector partnerships where local organizations lead screening efforts in their own communities. Offers an innovative approach to preventive screening that achieves greater efficiency and broader reach than traditional clinics. Simulation Training Improves the quality of care in rural healthcare facilities by providing advanced training in specialized medical services. Enhances workforce capabilities and increases patient volumes for local providers while reducing required travel times. Ensures patients receive appropriate treatment close to home to successfully reduce overcrowding at larger tertiary care hospitals. A goal of this initiative is to increase the amount of simulation training offered each year and to create and implement additional programs in other specialties. $203.40M Budget Period 1 Funding

Alaska.initiatives_raw: Alaska $272.65M Budget Period 2 Funding Initiative Name Initiative Description Healthy Beginnings Strengthens Alaska's maternal, infant, and early childhood health system as a foundation for healthy families, particularly in rural and frontier areas. Funds will expand access to prenatal and postpartum care closer to home, strengthen family-centered home visiting and early intervention services, and build healthy lifestyle programs that promote prevention and resilience from birth through adolescence. Health Care Access Strengthens primary, behavioral, oral, specialty, emergency, long-term, and post-acute care by: expanding integrated primary/behavioral/oral health; improving specialty access via telehealth, remote monitoring, and mobile teams; bolstering rural hospital capacity for 24/7 urgent, emergency, labor & delivery, and trauma care; supporting seniors and people with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD) to access aging-in-place and home- and community-based services; and improving post-acute and recovery care at home or in the community. Healthy Communities Advances prevention and chronic disease management across Alaska’s rural, remote, and frontier regions. It strengthens locally tailored primary and preventive care, expands digital tools and population health infrastructure for early intervention, and promotes healthy lifestyles through nutrition, physical activity, and community wellness programs. Pay for Value Supports Alaska's transition from fee-for-service to sustainable, value-based payment models that reward quality, coordination, and prevention. It builds the financial and operational foundation rural providers need to thrive under new reimbursement approaches by testing primary care and hospital payment models, evaluating readiness for the Center for Medicare and Medicaid Innovation (CMMI) Achieving Healthcare Efficiency through Accountable Design (AHEAD) Model, and creating alternative payment structures for integrated, high-value care. $272.17M Budget Period 1 Funding

Arizona.initiatives_raw: Arizona $165.01M Budget Period 2 Funding Initiative Name Initiative Description Rural Health Workforce Development and Training Program Deploys a comprehensive, multi-pronged strategy to recruit, train, and retain skilled health professionals in rural areas. Prioritizes non- physician providers such as allied health professionals, community health workers, nurses, and physician assistants. Invests subsequently in the primary and specialty care physician workforce to meet urgent community needs. Priority Health Initiatives Grants Portfolio Advances health outcomes across Arizona by funding high-impact, community-driven programs for screening and preventive care. Targets key areas including behavioral health, chronic disease prevention, and maternal-fetal health disparities. Partners with local organizations to deliver these critical resources directly to the communities that need them most. Making Rural Healthcare Accessible Expands access to primary and secondary preventive services via expansion of telehealth service availability, implementation of mobile/satellite service. Focuses on removing geographic barriers to ensure individuals receive necessary medical attention. Replicates proven outreach strategies to connect underserved populations with essential clinical providers. Making Rural Healthcare Resilient Builds and strengthens collaborations among rural health facilities and other local providers to improve operational efficiency. Promotes the active adoption of shared service models, co-located community hubs, and integrated networks. Establishes robust regional partnerships to help these smaller facilities survive and thrive. $166.99M Budget Period 1 Funding

Arkansas.initiatives_raw: Arkansas $207.79M Budget Period 2 Funding Initiative Name Initiative Description Healthy Eating, Active Recreation, & Transformation (HEART) Improves the health of rural Arkansans by increasing access to nutritious foods, physical activities, and preventative healthcare services. This effort leverages successful national strategies like the Centers for Disease Control’s (CDC) "Active People, Healthy Nation" program alongside existing local community health coalition frameworks. Success relies on critical partnerships with local public-school systems, community-based faith organizations, regional food distribution networks, and local healthcare clinics. Promoting Access, Coordination, and Transformation (PACT) Strengthens healthcare delivery in rural Arkansas by expanding specialty care, preventive screenings, and telehealth services. This program builds upon locally driven Clinically Integrated Networks (CIN) to encourage collaboration and resource sharing amongrural hospitals and clinics. Success relies on deep partnerships with state agencies, rural hospitals, local clinics, community organizations, and professional licensing boards Recruitment, Innovation, Skills, and Education for Arkansas (RISE AR) Builds a strong and skilled healthcare workforce to serve the unique needs of rural Arkansas families. This initiative expands medical residency programs and professional training slots by mimicking successful graduate medical education frameworks. Execution relies on critical partnerships with local medical schools, rural hospital systems, community health clinics, and state licensing boards. T elehealth, Health- Monitoring, and Response Innovation for Vital Expansion (THRIVE) Expands digital healthcare access across rural communities through advanced remote monitoring systems and emergency dispatch upgrades. This strategy modernizes existing emergency medical infrastructure and utilizes home health technology to support patients managing chronic diseases. Success relies on crucial partnerships with local paramedics, rural healthcare networks, emergency response coordinators, and technology providers. $208.78M Budget Period 1 Funding

Colorado.initiatives_raw: Colorado $197.16M Budget Period 2 Funding Initiative Name Initiative Description Transforming Rural Care: Hospitals and Chronic Disease Prevention Focuses on providing educational, disease prevention, and care coordination services for high-priority chronic conditions. This initiative supports rural hospitals and providers by helping them hire and train staff dedicated to improving care coordination. The program leverages partnerships with rural and critical access hospitals, rural health clinics and providers, Federally Qualified Health Centers(FQHCs), community-based organizations, Colorado Social Health Information Exchange (CoSHIE) hubs, regional health alliances, workforce development partners, and organizations offering training and technical assistance to deliver high-quality prevention services. Build Data and Evaluation Infrastructure for Chronic Disease Programs Strengthens data systems and performance monitoring to ensure chronic disease programs are effective and sustainable. This initiative creates a unified approach for collecting and analyzing data across programs and regions, enabling real-time feedback. It supports rural providers by providing technical assistance to ensure data interoperability and alignment with state and federal standards and implements a standardized performance monitoring and evaluation framework to track reach, outcomes, and return on investment for rural prevention programs. Build and Connect Colorado’s Rural Health Networks Establishes coordination and collaboration across Colorado's rural health system by building regional health networks. This initiative connects hospitals, clinics, and local public health agencies to improve access, quality, and long-term system resilience. It supports Tribal participation by helping them create their own rural health networks. Strengthen Rural Care Delivery Systems Transforms rural-care delivery systems by improving EMS coverage and expanding care coordination. This initiative enhances the capacity of rural providers to deliver timely and sustainable high-quality care in their communities. It supports collaborative care networks that integrate rural hospitals, rural health clinics, and behavioral health providers with shared electronic medical record systems, referral management, care coordination positions, and joint protocols for acute-care transitions. Sustain Rural Hospital Operations and Regulatory Readiness Ensures the long-term stability and operational capacity of rural hospitals across Colorado. This initiative provides direct financial support to rural hospitals facing financial, operational, and workforce challenges. It enables hospitals to procure technical assistance and targeted operational support to realign or sustain essential service lines, enable regulatory readiness, invest in small-scale infrastructure improvements, and support strategic planning and implementation. $200.11M Budget Period 1 Funding

Connecticut.initiatives_raw: Connecticut $153.65M Budget Period 2 Funding Initiative Name Initiative Description Population Health Outcomes Facilitates access to prevention, primary care, dental, and behavioral health. Builds simple entry points to care in community settings by strengthening the capacity of primary care clinics, community health centers, rural health clinics, behavioral health providers, tele- behavioral services, EMS and community teams, schools, senior centers, parks, and other local organizations. Supports mobile health delivery, operationalizing new primary care and dental vans for rural and Tribal communities. Establishes a local facilitatoror hub to convene partners and implement strategies that promote access to school-based mental health resources and referral, expand preventive services for older adults, promote active living through community assets, and strengthen behavioral health support. Improvesaccess to mental health supports and emergency department (ED) diversion for adults. Extends the Family Bridge universal nurse and community health worker home visiting program for newborns and postpartum women. Workforce Expands education and training opportunities, aligning licensure and certification standards, and improving recruitment and retention across levels of care. Builds accessible training programs with certifications that transfer easily between care settings. Expands clinical placements, modernizing training curricula, and removing barriers to employment in rural areas. Invests in coordinated strategies that strengthen training pipelines, remove practice barriers to education, and enhance career development opportunities. Data and Technology Expands statewide Health Information Exchange (HIE) participation, building shared technology infrastructure, and supporting innovative data tools that connect providers, improve care coordination, and ensure access to modern health systems for rural residents.Through collaboration with the Office of Policy and Management (formerly Office of Health Strategy (OHS)), Department of Public Health (DPH), Department of Social Services (DSS), and Connecticut’s statewide HIE, Connie, the initiative creates a fully integrated data ecosystem that enables providers to share information, track outcomes, and respond quickly to patient needs. Hospitals, Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs), long-term care providers, behavioral health providers, and EMS will be better connected through shared tools for population health management, event notification, and predictive analytics. These systems will improve care coordination, reduce unnecessary ED use, and support proactive outreach and chronic disease management in rural settings. Care Transformation and Stability Strengthens the foundation of rural healthcare by supporting infrastructure and right-sizing support, improving care coordination, as well as supporting value-based models and sustainable financing strategies. Supports integrated systems of care that expand access to community-based services, reduce reliance on hospital-based interventions, and improve financial resilience for local providers.Supports the development of 23-hour adult crisis stabilization units that provide short-term, non-hospital crisis care in safe, home-like environments. $154.25M Budget Period 1 Funding

Delaware.initiatives_raw: Delaware $160.29M Budget Period 2 Funding Initiative Name Initiative Description Rural “Hope Center” Initiative Replicates the successful Hope Center model to serve rural residents experiencing homelessness with serious mental illness and substance use disorder in Kent and Sussex Counties. Establishes two new centers in through the strategic renovation, staffing, and equipping of existing state-owned facilities, transforming underutilized infrastructure into comprehensive, integrated hubs for healthcare, behavioral health, and housing stability services. These centers will offer critical non congregate temporary housing, including at least 20 transitional beds specifically for individuals with serious mental illness and substance use disorder, plus safe individual and family units. The centers will strengthen the rural service network and support upstream drivers of health by bringing essential health, behavioral health, and housing supports together in communities where access to these services are limited. Rural Community Health Hubs Establishes a network of mobile health units and brick-and-mortar community health hubs to deliver preventive, chronic, and specialty care to underserved communities in rural Sussex and Kent Counties. Awards fund local health systems, community organizations, and health technology partners to deploy staff, equip, and operate mobile health units and brick-and-mortar community health hubs. Mobile health units will be strategically deployed to familiar, accessible community locations including schools, churches, town centers, and community parking lots, bringing medical services directly to rural residents where they live and gather, especially for physically disabled and elderly residents. School-Based Health Centers Expansion Initiative Expands Delaware’s network of school-based health centers (SBHCs) by establishing four new SBHCs in rural Sussex County middle schools to provide comprehensive physical, behavioral, and preventive health services directly to students, eliminating transportation barriers and improving access to primary care, mental health services, behavioral risk assessments, chronic disease management, and nutrition counseling. Supports minor building renovations to establish clinical space (exam rooms, counseling offices, screening areas), purchase equipment and supplies, and establish operations. Food is Medicine (FIM) Infrastructure Initiative Institutes a FIM infrastructure in rural Kent and Sussex counties to address high rates of hypertension and diabetes among food-insecure older adults. Hires 4-5 community health workers and registered dietitians to serve patients in rural health practices across Kent and Sussex. Deploys Electronic Medical Record (EMR)-decision support tools for participating providers, a telehealth nutrition consultation platform, a patient-facing mobile application, and remote patient monitoring systems. Certifies 15 Culinary Medicine Teachers totrain 150 rural practitioners (70% rural serving) and implements of a pilot for 375 participants with diabetes or hypertension. Develops coding, billing, and payment approaches to integrate FIM services into Delaware Medicaid and value-based care arrangements. Pilots a high school work- based learning program for students to gain hands-on experience in FIM interventions. $157.39M Budget Period 1 Funding

Georgia.initiatives_raw: Georgia $221.73M Budget Period 2 Funding Initiative Name Initiative Description Transforming for a Sustainable Health System Prepares rural healthcare facilities and providers to qualify for the national Achieving Healthcare Efficiency through Accountable Design (AHEAD) model for value-based care. This initiative focuses on achieving long-term financial stability for rural hospitals by assessing readiness, identifying gaps, and providing technical support and grants. It involves collaboration with various providers, hospitals, and community organizations to transform how healthcare is delivered and paid for in rural areas. Strengthening the Continuum of Care Addresses healthcare gaps for rural Georgians across all life stages. This initiative improves the health of children and families by creating better links between schools, community behavioral health, and primary care providers. It also expands crucial services like newborn screenings, emergency transportation, support for brain injury survivors, and increases access to nutrition services for children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and pregnant women. Connecting to Care to Improve Healthcare Access Closes gaps in access to quality healthcare for rural populations through innovation and technology. This effort deploys mobile health clinics and telehealth pods to bring primary, specialty, dental, behavioral, and preventive care directly to communities. It also strengthens perinatal care and enhances telehealth services through partnerships with rural hospitals, clinics, and public health departments. Growing a Highly Skilled Healthcare Workforce Strengthens the healthcare workforce in rural Georgia through focused education, training, and retention programs. The initiative provides educational awards, residencies, and financial incentives to encourage doctors, nurses, and other clinicians to practice in rural areas. It uses partnerships with academic institutions and health systems to build a sustainable pipeline of skilled providers for underserved communities. Leveraging T echnology for Healthcare Innovations Creates a modern and efficient healthcare system by integrating new technologies. This initiative improves patient data security, enhances electronic medical records, and provides funding for new health technologies incorporating solutions such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), cybersecurity, robotics, and electronic medical records. It supports rural hospitals and clinics by using technology to improve patient care, expand access, and increase data sharing among providers. Rural Technology Catalyst Fund to be implemented in Y ear 2 $218.86M Budget Period 1 Funding

Hawaii.initiatives_raw: Hawai’i Initiative Name Initiative Description Rural Health Information Network (RHIN) Connects rural hospitals, clinics, and Native Hawaiian health centers to the rest of the state through a modern, statewide digital backbone. Integrates interoperable electronic health records, wireless networks, and data hubs to facilitate secure data exchange. Enables seamless care coordination and practice transformation across independent providers. Pili Ola T elehealth Network Connects rural communities directly to healthcare providers by establishing a comprehensive, statewide telehealth network. Integrates digital health access, virtual care, and clinical telehealth training into underserved areas. Improves healthcare delivery bybridging geographic barriers to match local patients with specialized medical professionals. Rural Infrastructure for Care Access (RICA) Expands physical EMS and bolsters the existing behavioral health infrastructure in rural communities. Implements evidence-based community care practices by expanding healthcare teams, community paramedicine, and mobile healthcare units. Increases immediate care access to improve patient outcomes and reduce regional disparities. Hawai'i Outreach for Medical Education in Rural Under-resourced Neighborhoods (HOME RUN) Expands the education, recruitment, and retention of healthcare workers across rural Hawai'i through a robust pipeline-to-practice initiative. Offers tailored certificate programs, residency opportunities, educational awards, and financial incentives to build the local workforce. Delivers structured mentoring and professional support to encourage clinicians to establish practices in underserved areas. $189.62M Budget Period 2 Funding $188.89M Budget Period 1 Funding

Idaho.initiatives_raw: Idaho $182.70M Budget Period 2 Funding Initiative Name Initiative Description Improving Rural Access T o Care Through Technology Strengthens the foundation of rural care through investments in telehealth, shared infrastructure, and cybersecurity. This initiative improves care delivery for rural citizens by equipping healthcare facilities like Rural Health Clinics (RHCs), Critical Access Hospitals (CAHs), and Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) with modern technology. It requires collaboration between healthcare systems, treatment centers, and long-term care facilities to successfully implement these upgrades. Ensuring Accessible Quality Care Through Innovative Models Extends healthcare services to geographically isolated areas using innovative and technology enabled care models. This effortuses health extenders, such as community health workers and community health emergency medical services (CHEMS) professionals, to providecare in home and community settings. The initiative relies on partnerships with EMS agencies, post secondary institutions, and community employers to expand the healthcare workforce. Sustaining Rural Workforce With Training, Recruitment, And Retention Builds a skilled rural health workforce by offering financial incentives, new training pathways, and community support. The initiative targets a wide range of healthcare professionals, from students to established providers, by offering incentives including educational awards, retention bonuses, and expanded medical education programs. Success depends on partnerships with educational institutions, healthcare facilities, and community-based organizations. Implement Population Specific, Evidence-Based Projects To Make America Healthy Again Advances rural health by implementing prevention and treatment programs for chronic disease, behavioral health, and maternal and child health. This initiative serves rural populations by using proven, evidence-based models to improve health outcomes and build local capacity for care. It requires partnerships with a broad range of stakeholders, including healthcare providers, school systems, and community organizations. Investing In Rural Health Infrastructure And Partnerships Addresses the need for sustainable access to rural healthcare through investments in facility renovations, clinical equipment, and partnerships. The initiative focuses on modernizing healthcare facilities to support innovative care delivery and specializedservices for rural communities. Key partnerships include tribal nations, pharmacies, and various healthcare systems and clinics. $185.97M Budget Period 1 Funding

Illinois.initiatives_raw: Illinois Initiative Name Initiative Description Hospital Transformation Modernizes the rural healthcare delivery system to improve the long-term financial viability of rural hospitals. This initiativebuilds upon the Illinois' Health Transformation Collaboratives (HTCs) model to establish regional partnerships, transform service lines, and develop sustainable, high quality care models for rural residents. Key stakeholders include the four existing rural HTCs, rural hospitals, and various healthcare providers and community organizations. Community Care Infrastructure Strengthens primary and behavioral healthcare in rural regions to reduce fragmentation and improve access to care. This initiative provides targeted funding to providers to implement integrated, team-based care models, such as the Collaborative Care Model (CoCM), and enhance care coordination. It requires partnerships with organizations like the Illinois Primary Health Care Association (IPHCA) and the Community Behavioral Health Association (CBHA) to distribute funds and provide oversight Hospital Disease Prevention Supports rural hospitals in implementing disease prevention programming for the communities they serve. This initiative directs hospitals to use community health needs assessments to identify local health priorities and deploy evidence-based interventions for conditions like diabetes and mental health. The Illinois Critical Access Hospital Network (ICAHN) will administer funds to rural hospitals based on the population size of their service area. EMS and Mobile Healthcare Addresses the lack of available transportation and healthcare shortages in rural areas by funding mobile healthcare models. This initiative enhances rural EMS by expanding services like community paramedicine, leveraging the Chicago EMS Mobile Integrated Healthcare Community Paramedicine (MIH-CP) model. It involves partnerships with the Illinois Department of Public Health (IDPH) and Resource Hospitals to build the necessary infrastructure and support for mobile health services. $190.46 Budget Period 2 Funding $193.42M Budget Period 1 Funding

The MOCC aims to ensure rural communities get timely access to trauma, stroke, psychiatric and maternal care by streamlining referrals, reducing inappropriate emergency room (ER) use, supporting rural hospital sustainability and strengthening preparedness for mass casualty events. Growing Community Connections through Indiana 211 Launches Indiana Community Connect, a coordinated care network designed to help people in rural communities access essential resources more easily. Iowa.initiatives_raw: Iowa $216.01M Budget Period 2 Funding Initiative Name Initiative Description Hometown Connections Strengthens care coordination and service delivery in rural areas through strategic partnerships among healthcare providers. The initiative targets rural residents by leveraging partnerships with regional hospitals to address persistent gaps in care. This initiative expands an existing hub-and-spoke model, which Iowa refers to as Centers of Excellence. Additionally, new Health Hub and Spoke programs and school-based services programs are developed. Combat Cancer: Prevent and Treat Reduces the burden of cancer in rural communities through investments in prevention, screening, and treatment strategies. This initiative expands access to care through a Health Hub model, focusing on lung, breast, colon, and skin cancers. The program leverages partnerships and rural provider networks to address longstanding gaps in cancer care. Communities of Care Addresses challenges in accessing coordinated, person-centered care by piloting co-located service delivery sites. The initiative enhances care coordination by embedding community health workers (CHWs) to help with chronic disease prevention. This program targets rural Iowans by partnering with local public health agencies, Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs), and hospitals. Health Information Exchange Sustains and expands the Iowa Health Information Exchange (HIE) to transform rural healthcare delivery. This initiative improves care coordination by connecting rural providers to patient data across different electronic medical record platforms. The program targets rural hospitals and clinics by leveraging partnerships with behavioral health providers, FQHCs, and local health departments. Emergency Medical Service (EMS) Community Care Mobile Transforms prehospital care by strengthening the EMS workforce and integrating telehealth and home-based services through an EMS system development and sustainability assessment, mobile integrated health care, and the High-risk Obstetrics (OB) and Neonatal Transport Project. Reduces unnecessary emergency room visits and targets rural Iowans by leveraging partnerships with local EMS agencies to improve maternal and neonatal outcomes. $209.04M Budget Period 1 Funding

Kansas.initiatives_raw: Kansas $225.90M Budget Period 2 Funding Initiative Name Initiative Description Expand Primary and Secondary Prevention Programs Achieves meaningful reductions in chronic disease and preventable hospitalizations for rural residents. This initiative deploys Community Health Workers (CHWs) and expands mobile cancer screenings to address the root causes of disease. The program leverages successful models like Food is Medicine (FIM) and Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly (PACE), and partners with the Care Collaborative and Kansas State University to serve its target population. Secure Local Access to Primary Care Ensures rural Kansans have access to financially stable healthcare providers in their local communities. This initiative provides grants for regional partnerships, supports the conversion of facilities to rural emergency hospitals (REHs), and improves revenue cycles. It leverages partnerships with the Kansas Hospital Association and urban not-for-profit health systems to strengthen the state's rural delivery system. Build a Sustainable Rural Health Workforce Addresses provider shortages by creating a robust pipeline of healthcare professionals trained and incentivized to practice in rural Kansas. This initiative establishes rural physician residency programs and expands educational awards for students in high-demand allied health fields. The program partners with Kansas colleges and universities to offer career exploration programs and create a homegrown workforce. Enable Value-Based Care Transitions rural providers from a fee-for-service system to a value-based model that rewards quality outcomes and care coordination. This initiative offers financial incentives for adopting evidence-based practices and prepares providers to participate in Accountable Care Organizations (ACOs). The program leverages the state's Medicaid managed care organizations (MCOs) and a "shadow" ACO to support providers in this transition. Harness Data and T echnology Empowers rural providers to improve patient care by expanding the use of telehealth, remote patient monitoring, and data analytics. This initiative provides telehealth navigators to coordinate specialty care and establishes a data infrastructure program to enhance providers' ability to use data effectively. It partners with the Care Collaborative to deploy nurses trained as telehealth navigators inprimary care practices. $221.90M Budget Period 1 Funding

Kentucky.initiatives_raw: Kentucky $211.33M Budget Period 2 Funding Initiative Name Initiative Description Chronic Care Innovations: Rural Community Hubs, Community Health Workers (CHWs), and Data and T echnology Strategy Enhances chronic care innovation, starting with obesity and diabetes, through local community hubs designed to scale evidence-based interventions and explore digital health supports such as AI-enabled self-management coaching across the lifespan. Unites fragmented interventions, programs, resources, and technology tools for local community organizations to enable coordinated chronic disease management. Rural Community Hubs are locally led at a regional level to align rural health stakeholders on shared priorities.Expands the CHW workforce through training opportunities. Enhances existing state-based resources for clinical care management and non-clinical resource coordination including closed loop referrals. Creates a Learning Collaborative to define desired data and technologycapabilities needed to support continuous learning to improve rural health. PoWERing Rural Maternal and Infant Health: Community-based Teams Enables timely initiation of quality, perinatal care from early pregnancy, postpartum and maternity care deserts through a network of coordinated telehealth-enabled maternal care teams. Establishes a scalable, patient-centered, and community-based model to address access to maternity and infant care in maternity care deserts. Leverages the PoWER (People Who Work for Engagement and Resilience) Team model with doulas, perinatal CHWs, and peer support specialists to provide essential services to mothers and infants during pregnancy and the first year following the end of the pregnancy. Rapid Response to Recovery: EmPATHModel, Mobile Crisis and T elehealth Provides person-centered, technology-enabled access to integrated crisis care, linking EMS, behavioral health providers, and mobile crisis units through shared data and referral platforms. Builds on Kentucky's existing Emergency Psychiatric Assessment, Treatment and Healing (EmPATH) model and Mobile Crisis Intervention services. Creates an integrated, interoperable system that supports individualsthrough the behavioral health crisis continuum reducing system reliance on first responders. Utilizes telehealth technology and mobile crisis services to improve emergency response and ongoing patient recovery. Rooted in Health: Rural Dental Access Program Expands dental hygiene and dental assistant training, externship programs, and mobile/tele-dental hubs to address unmet oral health needs. Improves dental care in rural communities through comprehensive workforce development and expanded community access points, including advanced dental extraction training for rural dentists. Supports local providers by integrating tele-dentistry tools, establishing a statewide tele-dental network, and expanding mobile/portable dental care units. Reduces avoidable emergency department visits for non-emergent dental pain through proactive, community-based dental services. $212.91M Budget Period 1 Funding

Louisiana.initiatives_raw: Louisiana $211.86M Budget Period 2 Funding Initiative Name Initiative Description Strengthen Health and Emergency Systems through Workforce Expansion and Integration Addresses critical healthcare shortages and slow emergency response times in rural Louisiana through a three-part strategy. Expands the local workforce using financial incentives, tax credits, and educational partnerships to build a sustainable training pipeline. Enhances emergency response capacity in underserved parishes by launching community paramedicine and tele-EMS pilots. Modernize T echnology Infrastructure and Capacity for Efficiency and Care Coordination Integrates four key strategies to build a secure, interoperable health technology network using modern Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) and standardized data frameworks. Partnering with Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs), schools, and libraries helps expand community digital literacy so all residents can participate. Collaborating with national partners like the National Academy for State Health Policy accelerates cross-state data sharing and public-private investment. Reinforce Innovative, Outcomes-Based Care Delivery in Rural Areas Launches risk-sharing and value-based payment arrangements to help rural hospitals, Accountable Care Organizations (ACOs), and FQHCs deliver better coordinated care. Supports high-impact, non-billable care models like care navigation and transitional services that reduce expensive emergency visits. Integrates these payment innovations into existing Medicaid and managed-care frameworks to create a sustainable, performance-driven reimbursement system. Expand Physical Activity and Nutrition Interventions Through Community-Based Partnerships Tackles high rates of food insecurity and chronic disease in rural areas by prioritizing preventive care and addressing non-clinical barriers. Employs a two-pronged approach that features direct nutrition interventions through food FARMacies alongside broad fitness programs. Integrates these community-based health models to sustainably improve overall population health and care coordination. Louisiana is also implementing a Rural Technology Catalyst Fund, which promotes consumer-facing, technology-driven solutions for chronic disease prevention and management in rural populations. $208.37M Budget Period 1 Funding

Maine.initiatives_raw: Maine $190.36M Budget Period 2 Funding Initiative Name Initiative Description Population Health: Promoting Timely Access T o High-Quality Care Promotes timely access to high-quality care for rural Mainers facing complex health challenges, including aging residents and those with chronic conditions. This initiative expands mobile services, establishes more School Based Health Centers (SBHCs), and improves access to substance use disorder treatments. The plan requires collaboration with schools, healthcare providers, and Tribal governments to better coordinate care. Workforce: Strengthening Maine's Rural Health Workforce Strengthens Maine's rural health workforce to address provider shortages that limit access to care. It aims to grow the pipeline of health workers through new training programs and offers financial incentives to attract and retain clinicians in rural communities. The initiative partners with health employers and state education systems to establish successful career exploration models and build K-12 talent pipelines. Provides customized training through the Healthcare Training for ME (HTFM), which includes a centralized portal for health employers to share their training needs and access workforce resources, rural training labs, and mobile simulation units. T echnology: Modernizing Rural Care Delivery With Digital Health T echnology Modernizes rural care delivery by enabling providers and patients to benefit from technology and information advances. This effort expands access to telehealth, upgrades electronic medical record systems, and supports the adoption of artificial intelligence applications. Telehealth activities include a virtual quick (urgent) care program, tele-behavioral health (Tele-BH) program targeted to youth and perinatal care, on-demand specialty telehealth services for special populations, and provider-to-provider specialty on-demand (synchronous) consultations. Access: Bridging The Healthcare Affordability Gap For Rural Mainers Addresses financial and transportation barriers to healthcare experienced by rural Mainers. It includes providing payments toreimburse for uncompensated care and using technology to help residents select the best value health coverage. The initiative will also improve coordination of existing transportation solutions. Sustainable Rural Health Ecosystems: Addressing Financial Instability Of Rural Providers Supports the long-term financial strength and resilience of Maine's rural health ecosystem. Provides tailored support to hospitals facing financial challenges, helps develop regional structures for improved payment models, and expands the service continuum. Fundscapital improvements and technology to help rural providers strengthen their financial stability. Develops regional structures to support improved alternative payment models (APMs) through capital investments and technical assistance. $190.01M Budget Period 1 Funding

Maryland.initiatives_raw: Maryland Initiative Name Initiative Description Transform the Rural Health Workforce Develops a strong health workforce in rural communities by expanding existing efforts and implementing new ones to recruit and retain healthcare clinicians and allied health professionals. It leverages Maryland's existing Registered Apprenticeship program andArea Health Education Centers (AHECs), and requires key partnerships with the Maryland Department of Labor, the state School of Medicine,and healthcare providers. Promote Sustainable Access and Innovative Care for Rural Marylanders Expands access to healthcare services for rural Marylanders by supporting the growth of primary and specialty care practices in rural communities. The initiative focuses on increasing primary and behavioral health capacity, improving the efficiency of local health agencies, and strengthening emergency trauma response. It builds upon Maryland's experience with value-based care models and involves key partnerships with the Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC), Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC), local health departments, school-based health centers, the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems (MIEMSS), and the state’s designated health information exchange. Empower Rural Marylanders to Eat for Health Improves access to nutritious, locally grown foods for rural Marylanders by investing in infrastructure and creating demand for healthy foods. This initiative will expand cold storage facilities, support small grocers and mobile markets, and provide nutrition education to residents in rural areas. The program builds and leverages grant programming and will be executed through partnerships with the Maryland Department of Agriculture, the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Maryland Department of Emergency Management, Rural Maryland Council, and local health departments. $168.41M Budget Period 2 Funding $168.18M Budget Period 1 Funding

Massachusetts.initiatives_raw: Massachusetts $158.39M Budget Period 2 Funding Initiative Name Initiative Description Population Health Advancement Improves clinical management of chronic disease through enhanced clinical and community coordination. This initiative expands participation in value-based payment models and creates stronger linkages between rural providers. The program will advance rural population health, improve quality of care, and increase efficiencies to lower healthcare costs. Innovation in Rural Care Models Advances rural-appropriate care models by standing up mobile health units and expanding telehealth services. This initiative supports the expansion of proven models and integrated specialty care networks to increase access for rural residents. Program investmentswill provide technical assistance and fund the infrastructure required to broaden service availability across these communities. Training Healthcare for Retention, Innovation, and Excellence (THRIVE) Strengthens the full continuum of the healthcare workforce in rural communities with targeted activities focused on workforce development, recruitment, and retention. This initiative will focus on programs that will attract, train, and support healthcare providers in rural areas. The programs are designed to encourage providers to commit to serving their rural communities for a minimum of 5years and thrive professionally. Healthy Rural Communities Empowers rural populations by expanding local organizations to deliver community-based chronic disease prevention. This initiative addresses the root causes of poor health by supporting proven, tailored educational programs. It leverages community networksto create critical linkages between these local prevention efforts and clinical care providers. Emergency Medical System (EMS) Service Integration Strengthens the viability and clinical role of EMS for rural communities. This initiative deploys a new prehospital protocol and medication dosing mobile application to improve the quality of care before patients reach the hospital. This initiative will support integrating new EMS services in rural areas to increase their role in providing clinical care. It will support healthcare efficiencies and new reimbursement mechanisms for ambulances while ultimately providing more operational stability to these local agencies and systems that provide critical services. Massachusetts is also implementing a Rural Technology Catalyst Fund, which promotes consumer-facing, technology-driven solutions for chronic disease prevention and management in rural populations. $162.01M Budget Period 1 Funding

Michigan.initiatives_raw: Michigan $170.61M Budget Period 2 Funding Initiative Name Initiative Description Transforming Rural Health through Partnerships Initiative Reimagines Michigan’s rural health landscape by piloting and scaling community oriented approaches to care leveraging Hubs that serve as points of collaboration to address health and social outcomes. The Hub will connect local, community and regional partnersutilizing Community Health Workers (CHWs), Community Information Exchange (CIE), Health Information Exchange (HIE), and Health in All Policies (HiAP) approaches to address root causes of disease. Workforce for Wellness Strengthens the rural health and wellness workforce through training, recruitment, and retention programs within rural Michigan. The initiative provides training for professionals including behavioral health, maternal health, EMS, primary care, and other high need specialists. Pipeline programs, stipends, and educational awards will support current workers in rural communities while increasing the number of health professionals. Interoperability in Action Enhances the technical infrastructure and interoperability of health data in Michigan’s rural areas by investing in electronic health record (EHR systems, clinical and administrative technology, HIE and CIE capability. Pilot programs will link EMS data with EHR systems to patient improve care coordination. At the onset, the initiative will connect partners from various sectors including rural providers, and IT experts to develop statewide standards for data sharing and integration. Care Closer to Home Blueprint Creates sustainable, community-based pathways that bring health services closer to where people live and work. By promoting innovations that improve chronic disease management, maternal and child health, and behavioral health outcomes, the initiative aims to make care more efficient, coordinated, and person-centered. The initiative will connect disparate partners within health and social sectors. $173.13M Budget Period 1 Funding

Minnesota.initiatives_raw: Minnesota $193.83M Budget Period 2 Funding Initiative Name Initiative Description Community-Based Preventive Care and Chronic Disease Management Supports rural hospitals, clinics, and Tribal health organizations in providing preventive care for chronic diseases to Minnesotans living in rural areas. This initiative increases access to screenings and self-management tools by building on existing programs like the Minnesota 2035 Plan and community care hubs. Executing this initiative requires collaboration with local public health departments, community organizations, and technical assistance providers. Recruit and Retain Talent in Rural Communities Addresses workforce shortages by creating pathways for students and incumbent workers to enter and advance in rural healthcare careers. This initiative targets high school students and existing rural workers, leveraging "Earn and Train" apprenticeship models and expanding rural clinical rotations. Key partnerships include Minnesota State Colleges and Universities, rural hospitals, clinics, and the University of Minnesota Medical School. Sustain Access to Services to Keep Care Closer to Home Encompasses technology-focused solutions, mobile care delivery, and integration of underused, community-embedded frontline health care team members such as community health workers (CHWs), community health representatives (CHRs), doulas, peer support specialists, and community paramedics in community and clinical settings in a financially sustainable way. The initiative focuses on rural residents who face barriers to care by expanding telehealth access points and mobile physical and oral health units. Create Regional Care Models to Improve Whole Person Health Supports collaborative regional activities to improve access to timely and appropriate health care, with a focus on essentialobstetrics and mental health services. Develops provider-to-provider telehealth linkages that provide access to professional services not available in the immediate community and connect primary care providers to specialist expertise when needed. Establishes provider-to-provider learning and support networks using simulation training for obstetrics and Extension for Community Healthcare Outcomes (ECHO) programs to improve clinical knowledge, reduce professional isolation, and strengthen the quality of care in underserved regions, keeping patients close to home. $193.09M Budget Period 1 Funding

Mississippi.initiatives_raw: Mississippi $204.68M Budget Period 2 Funding Initiative Name Initiative Description Statewide Rural Health Assessment Conducts a comprehensive assessment of rural health needs to confirm and improve the state's existing plan. Engages ≥150 stakeholders across hospitals, Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs), EMS, behavioral health, and community representatives. Identifies ≥5 major service, workforce, or infrastructure gaps statewide and deliver a data-driven roadmap with recommendations aligned with assessment findings, prioritized by urgency, impact, and feasibility. Coordinated Regional Integrated Systems (CRIS) Initiative Strengthens regional care networks and patient care continuity reduces low-acuity ER visits through nurse navigation and treat-in-place interventions. Engages rural hospitals and clinics in coordinated care networks, and ensures high-risk patients have completed care plans within 7 days of discharge, resulting in lower 30-day readmission rates for high-risk patients. Workforce Expansion Initiative (WEI) Strengthens the rural healthcare workforce to improve access and quality of care for residents. The program focuses on recruiting, training, and retaining a wide range of healthcare professionals in rural areas. It builds a sustainable workforce by formingpartnerships with local schools, community colleges, and vocational programs. Health Technology Advancement and Modernization (HTAM) Initiative Modernizes rural healthcare systems by improving the technology that supports quality care. Supports digital health by upgrading providers’ interoperable EHR systems, enabling eligible providers to actively share data through the statewide health information exchange Health Information Exchange (HIE). Provides applicable provider staff with cybersecurity or IT training, and patients with digital tools, including patient portals, telehealth, and remote monitoring. $205.91M Budget Period 1 Funding

Missouri.initiatives_raw: Missouri $218.55M Budget Period 2 Funding Initiative Name Initiative Description Regional Coordinating Networks and Hub Activation Establishes a network of 30 Local Community Hubs and seven Regional Coordinating Networks to improve care coordination for rural Missourians. This initiative builds on the state's Transformation of Rural Community Health Care (ToRCHCare) pilot program to improve access and health outcomes for residents across 104 rural counties by incentivizing organizations within the Hubs and Networks to continue collaboration. Alternative Payment Models Develops new payment models that reward rural providers for delivering high-quality, high-value care instead of just the volume of services. This program targets all rural providers and payers in Missouri, aiming to improve financial stability for a system where over half of rural hospitals operate at a loss. The initiative will leverage Missouri's Medicaid program and engage with commercial payers and Medicare Advantage plans to create sustainable financial incentives. Digital Backbone Creates a unified digital infrastructure to connect Missouri's fragmented rural health systems and enable secure data sharingamong providers. This initiative targets all rural providers, including hospitals, clinics, and pharmacies, by establishing a RuralHealth Data Collaborative and promoting interoperability. It builds on existing platforms including the Hospital Industry Data Institute (HIDI) and requires partnerships with EHR vendors, technology companies, and various state health departments. Rural Health Workforce Programs Builds a sustainable pipeline of healthcare professionals to serve in rural Missouri through coordinated recruitment, training, and retention efforts. The program targets students and existing healthcare workers expanding career education in high schools, launching maternal health workforce expansion programs, establishing more clerkship opportunities, and supporting EMS workforce development. This involves partnerships with the Department of Higher Education & Workforce Development, Missouri's medical schools, and local healthcare providers, and provides childcare access and housing supports for rural healthcare workers. Provider Transformation Strengthens the operational and technological capabilities of rural healthcare providers to ensure their long-term stability and improve patient care. This initiative focuses on rural providers needing to modernize tools and facilities, targeting those at risk of closure due to financial strain. It will be implemented through partnerships with Regional Coordinating Networks and Community Hubs to deploy innovations like Remote Patient Monitoring and Ambient AI for documentation. $216.28M Budget Period 1 Funding

Nebraska.initiatives_raw: Nebraska $219.25M Budget Period 2 Funding Initiative Name Initiative Description Make Rural Nebraska Healthy Again Through Food as Medicine Lowers obesity risk and prevents chronic diseases for rural Nebraskans by improving access to healthy foods and nutrition education. This initiative supports rural schools in transitioning to whole fresh foods through grants for kitchen modernization and establishing physical activity and wellness programs. It also leverages partnerships with the agriculture sector and educational institutions to promote healthy eating from a young age. Regionalized Rural Access and Navigation Builds a statewide system of regionalized care that ensures every rural resident can access the right services at the right time. This initiative addresses challenges in rural healthcare by coordinating emergency medical and perinatal care and embedding community health workers into local health departments. The program leverages partnerships with the Department of Veterans Affairs and local health organizations to improve access for all rural residents. Rural Workforce Acceleration Recruits, trains, and retains a resilient healthcare workforce to serve rural and frontier communities in Nebraska. The initiative provides financial incentives for providers who commit to practicing in rural areas and uses a virtual reality simulation network to offer advanced training. It establishes career pathways for Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) recipients to enter the healthcare field and introduces school-age students to medical careers. eHealth and Mobile Brings high-quality, technology-enabled healthcare to rural and frontier Nebraskans through mobile, remote, and eHealth solutions. This program deploys mobile clinics to provide maternal and infant care directly within maternity care deserts and brings urgent dental care to rural areas. It also helps community pharmacies use digital tools to manage chronic diseases and provides remote patient monitoring for individuals in their homes. Rural Emergency Behavioral Health Creates an integrated, community-based emergency behavioral health system to improve outcomes and reduce costs. The initiative partners with the Nebraska Medical Association to co-locate mental health professionals in rural primary care clinics and implement a behavioral health nursing home pilot. It also leverages telehealth technology to give law enforcement instant access to crisis professionals and retrofits existing facilities to increase crisis stabilization capacity. $218.53M Budget Period 1 Funding

Nevada.initiatives_raw: Nevada $182.40M Budget Period 2 Funding Initiative Name Initiative Description Rural Health Outcomes Accelerator Program Funds evidence-based initiatives to improve health outcomes for rural residents with chronic disease, behavioral health needs, and maternal or infant health challenges. This initiative expands value-based payment models and integrates community health workersinto coordinated care teams to improve patient outcomes. The program leverages a Rural Value Acceleration Network (RVAN) and partnerships with rural hospitals, clinics, and academic institutions. Nevada Rural Health System Flex Fund Modernizes and enhances existing facilities and infrastructure for Nevada's rural healthcare system. This initiative providesflexible funding for capital expenditures at rural clinics, hospitals, and EMS agencies to improve the quality, capacity, and sustainability of local care. The program encourages regional purchasing arrangements and partnerships with larger health systems to support self-sustaining models for delivering essential services. Workforce Recruitment & Rural Access Program (WRRAP) Attracts and retains physicians and other providers in rural areas through specific retention strategies and incentive programs under the WRRAP . This initiative builds a "Grow-Your-Own" pipeline by creating career pathways from high school and supporting local training programs and rural residencies. The program partners with rural hospitals, clinics, and academic institutions to address long-term workforce shortages. Rural Health Innovation & T echnology (RHIT) Grant Creates a more connected and secure system of care by funding new tech-enabled hybrid care solutions and remote patient monitoring. This initiative helps build the necessary infrastructure to expand the use of innovative telehealth services and supports front-line providers caring for patients with complex needs. It will prioritize technology solutions that are sustainable and operationally efficient in low- bandwidth environments for Nevada's rural communities. $179.93M Budget Period 1 Funding

New Hampshire.initiatives_raw: New Hampshire $204.31M Budget Period 2 Funding Initiative Name Initiative Description Population Health Invests in health infrastructure, care coordination, and community outreach to strengthen prevention-first care for rural residents. Replicates community-based nursing, mobile integrated health, and community health worker models. Launches the state's first Dual Eligible Special Needs Plan to better integrate care for individuals enrolled in both Medicaid and Medicare. Healthcare Access Expands evidence-based care coordination and disease management models to improve medical outcomes for rural New Hampshire residents. Increases access to primary, behavioral, oral, perinatal, and specialty care by using telehealth technologies. Expects to successfully raise the total number of behavioral health, dental, pharmacy, and community-based visits. Workforce Strengthens the rural healthcare workforce through a coordinated partnership between local high school career technical education programs, post-secondary institutions, and local healthcare providers. Creates clear career pathways from high school to graduate degrees, including a new family medicine residency program in Coos County. Addresses critical workforce retention issues by expanding training opportunities and improving access to local childcare. T echnology Modernizes care delivery across rural communities by deploying scalable, integrated technology solutions. Introduces artificial intelligence tools to streamline clinical decisions, real-time claims, and administrative authorizations. Financial Sustainability Strengthens the financial sustainability of the rural healthcare system by investing heavily in prevention-first and value-based care. Prepares local healthcare providers to transition into value-based and two-sided risk arrangements. Integrates clinical capacityand technical infrastructure to reduce hospital discharge barriers and maintain critical safety-net providers. $204.02M Budget Period 1 Funding

NEW HAMPSHIRE 
New Hampshire Total Budget Period 1 Award: 
$204,016,550.20 
Total Funds Put to Work: $204,016,550.20 (as of 7/31/2026) 
Initiative 1: Rural Population Health ($14,455,592.11) 
Consumer Tech Solutions ($2,272,695.50) 
▪ $2,272,695.50 for technology that helps rural residents access, navigate, and engage with healthcare and 
community-based services. Investments may include digital navigation, patient-facing tools, remote 
monitoring, closed-loop referral capabilities, and other technologies that connect individuals with clinical 
care, prevention services, and community supports. 
Fostering Collaboration ($5,000,000) 
▪ $5,000,000 for regional and statewide partnerships among healthcare providers, community-based 
organizations, public health partners, and other rural stakeholders to coordinate population health 
strategies. Funding may support convening, regional planning, shared infrastructure, referral networks, 
and development of sustainable clinical-community partnerships. 
Prevention and Chronic Disease ($7,182,896.61) 
▪ $7,182,896.61 for clinical and community-based population health strategies that prevent disease, 
improve chronic disease management, and address priority needs such as nutrition, maternal and child 
health, behavioral health prevention and early intervention, healthy aging, and physical activity. 
Investments may support evidence-based interventions, care coordination, community-based services, 
and partnerships that improve health outcomes in rural populations. 
Initiative 2: Rural Healthcare Access ($74,670,900.78) 
Appropriate Care Availability ($12,628,209.97) 
▪ $12,628,209.97 for expansion, preservation, and redesign of healthcare services so rural residents can 
receive the right care in the right setting. Investments may increase access to primary care, EMS, post-
acute and long-term care, specialty services, oral health, and other essential services while reducing 
avoidable emergency department use, hospital stays, and unnecessary transfers. 
Behavioral Health $11,800,000) 
▪ $11,800,000 for expanded access to behavioral health services and integration of behavioral health into 
rural care delivery. Investments may include Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic (CCBHC) 
expansion, crisis and transition services, integrated care models, workforce supports, technology, and 
other activities that improve timely access and continuity of behavioral healthcare. 
Capital Expenditures and Infrastructure ($13,601,103.33) 
▪ $13,601,103.33 for renovations and other allowable capital improvements that enable transformation of 
rural healthcare delivery. Priority investments include maintaining or increasing nursing facility bed 
capacity and supporting Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs), Community Mental Health Centers 
(CMHCs), emergency medical services (EMS) agencies, and other eligible providers with physical 
improvements needed to expand access, implement new models of care, and improve patient flow 
across the healthcare continuum. 
Fostering Collaboration ($6,039,104.98) 
▪ $6,039,104.98 for supporting collaboration among rural providers, regional partners, payers, and 
implementation hubs to identify access barriers and develop shared solutions. Activities may include 
regional planning, provider convenings, shared service models, referral relationships, and coordination 
across primary care, behavioral health, EMS, hospitals, and post-acute care. 
Provider Payments $30,602,482.50) 
▪ $30,602,482.50 for supporting targeted payments to healthcare providers to implement and sustain new 
or expanded models of care that improve rural access. Investments may support primary care 
transformation, Mobile Integrated Health, specialty access, oral health, behavioral health, team-based 
 
NEW HAMPSHIRE 
care, and other delivery models where payment is necessary to enable implementation or bridge to a 
sustainable financing approach.  
Initiative 3: Rural Workforce Recruitment and Retention ($34,601,103.33) 
Behavioral Health ($6,000,000) 
▪ $6,000,000 for the development of the behavioral health workforce, including recruitment, education, 
training, clinical placement, and retention strategies. Investments may strengthen pipelines into 
behavioral health occupations and help CMHCs, CCBHCs, and other providers build the workforce 
needed to expand access and sustain new models of care. 
Capital Expenditures and Infrastructure ($13,601,103.33) 
▪ $13,601,103.33 for allowable educational and training infrastructure needed to expand rural healthcare 
workforce capacity. Investments may include simulation facilities, training equipment, learning 
environments, and other physical assets that increase the number of students who can enter and 
complete healthcare training programs. 
Workforce ($15,000,000) 
▪ $15,000,000 for recruitment, education, training, and retention of healthcare workers needed in rural 
communities. Investments through Community College System of New Hampshires (CCSNH), University 
System of New Hampshire (USNH), and other partners may expand nursing and other high-need training 
capacity, strengthen career pathways, support rural clinical experiences, develop employer partnerships, 
and increase the number of workers prepared to practice in rural settings.  
Initiative 4: Rural Health Technology ($29,940,939.25) 
Consumer Tech Solutions ($2,500,000) 
▪ $2,500,000 for patient-facing technology that improves access, care coordination, and engagement, 
including remote patient monitoring, telehealth access, digital navigation, and other tools that allow rural 
residents to connect with care and manage their health more effectively. 
IT Advances ($19,940,939.25) 
▪ $19,940,939.25 for modernization and integration of healthcare technology systems, including electronic 
health records (EHRs), interoperability, cybersecurity, data infrastructure, electronic dental records, EMS 
technology, and care management platforms. This includes Community Behavioral Health Association 
(CBHA)’s work to assess the technology environment across all 10 CMHCs and support coordinated 
selection of an EHR platform that strengthens care coordination and data sharing. 
Training and Technical Assistance ($7,500,000) 
▪ $7,500,000 for technical assistance to help healthcare organizations assess, select, implement, and 
optimize technology. Assistance may address EHRs, interoperability, cybersecurity, data reporting, digital 
workflow redesign, technology readiness, and adoption of tools that support clinical transformation and 
value-based care.  
Initiative 5: Rural Financial Solvency ($29,946,359.73) 
Capital Expenditures and Infrastructure ($13,601,103.33) 
▪ $13,601,103.33 for capital investments that improve both care delivery and financial sustainability, 
including nursing facility renovations that preserve or expand post-acute capacity, reduce hospital 
administrative stays by enabling timely discharge, and allow nursing facilities to serve more patients 
eligible for skilled nursing reimbursement. 
Fostering Collaboration ($14,452,751.40) 
▪ $14,452,751.40 for engagement among providers, payers, State agencies, and other partners to develop 
sustainable strategies. Activities include collaboration with NH Department of Health and Human 
Services (DHHS) Medicaid and Behavioral Health, Medicaid and Dental Managed Care Organizations, 
Critical Access Hospitals, FQHCs, EMS providers, the NH Insurance Department, and commercial payers 
to identify multi-payer approaches to coverage and alignment on reimbursement of services (e.g. 
 
NEW HAMPSHIRE 
comprehensive team-based primary care, mobile integrated health, CCBHC, value-based hospital 
reimbursement, etc.); inter-facility transport redesign work; projects to reduce hospital discharge barriers 
(e.g. streamlining Medicaid long-term care (LTC) eligibility processes, etc.). 
Innovative Care ($1,892,505) 
▪ $1,892,505 for the development and implementation of financially sustainable care-delivery and 
payment approaches, including value-based payment, alternative payment models, shared services, and 
other strategies that improve efficiency while maintaining or expanding rural access. Investments may 
include development of a Medicaid hospital payment model and other approaches designed to sustain 
transformation beyond Rural Health Transformation (RHT) funding. 
Program Operations ($20,401,655) 
Program Administration Expense ($20,401,655) 
▪ $20,401,655 for supporting the staffing, financial management, contracting, compliance, evaluation, 
reporting, governance, project management, and administrative infrastructure necessary to oversee the 
RHT Program. These expenses support the Governor’s Office of New Opportunities & Rural 
Transformational Health (GO-NORTH) Program and State responsibilities for federal grant administration, 
program integrity, monitoring, coordination, and accountability across all five initiatives.

New Mexico.initiatives_raw: New Mexico $211.04M Budget Period 2 Funding Initiative Name Initiative Description Healthy Horizons: Expanding Specialty Care Access and Chronic Disease Management Expands specialty care for rural and Tribal communities by using a combination of in-person visits, e-consults, and remote health tools. This approach strengthens chronic disease management for high-risk populations by improving prevention and integrating remote care solutions. Integrates behavioral health within chronic and maternal care networks, ensuring whole-person care across all rural and Tribal communities. Keeps care close to home and reduces unnecessary travel and delays in specialty care. Supports use of remote care tools (e.g., e-consults, telehealth, remote patient monitoring (RPM)) to expand access, support continuity, and reduce long travel times. Rooted in New Mexico: Building T omorrow's Rural Health Workforce Strengthens the recruitment, training, and retention of health professionals to ensure care remains local for rural, frontier, and Tribal communities. It builds on successful programs like FORWARD NM and Project ECHO (Extension for Community Healthcare Outcomes) to address workforce shortages and high turnover . The initiative fosters local interest in health careers by launching K-12 pathway programs and offering incentives for service commitments. Rural Health Innovation Fund: Enabling Community- Designed, Community-Led Change Establishes a grant program to support community-designed and community-led initiatives that respect and reflect the unique practices and priorities of different pueblos, Tribal nations, and rural communities. It provides opportunities for rural, frontier, and Tribal communities to address specific challenges that require local solutions. This fund allows providers and community-based organizations to apply for grants to address issues such as food insecurity, transportation, and preventive care. Bridge to Resilience: Rural Health Sustainability & Innovation Center (RHSIC) Supports financially distressed rural providers with tools and knowledge to operate more effectively and achieve sustainability. It delivers education and learning collaboratives focused on workforce recruitment, financial stability, and digital tools. This initiative helps providers by establishing new processes and training staff to carry best practices forward independently. RHSIC directly supports ruralproviders by coordinating and delivering high-impact technical assistance (e.g., operations, finance, service optimization, regional partnership coordination). Rural Health Data Hub: Establishing a Health Analytics Platform Builds a secure data infrastructure to enhance analytic capabilities, improve predictive analytics, and increase health data transparency across the state. Integrates patient information across medical, behavioral, and social services to promote a unified care experience for rural residents. The platform makes data available to consumers and providers to inform decision-making at the local, regional, and state levels. $211.48M Budget Period 1 Funding

New York.initiatives_raw: New York $207.75M Budget Period 2 Funding Initiative Name Initiative Description Rural Community Health Integration Strengthens the rural health safety net by building integrated health networks to enhance care delivery and coordination. This initiative encourages collaborative partnerships between rural hospitals, community providers, and other healthcare organizations. The program leverages the existing infrastructure of anchor institutions (institutions with demonstrated capacity and commitment in serving their constituents) to establish a path toward financial sustainability for all participating facilities. Strengthening Rural Communities with T echnology-Enhanced Primary Care Leverages historic investments in primary care by expanding the number of Patient-Centered Medical Home (PCMH)-recognized providers. This initiative helps rural practices adopt technology and advanced analytics to improve operational efficiency, quality, andfinancial sustainability. The program utilizes a cohort-based model to guide practices through PCMH recognition and implementation of technology- enabled workflows. Rural Roots: Building a Sustainable Rural Health care Workforce Addresses health care staffing shortages in rural communities by growing local talent and recruiting health professionals through multi-year service commitments. This initiative introduces students in grades 6-12 to health care careers and expands training opportunities at rural facilities. The program will build a data system that tracks health care workforce trends, needed specialties, and existing gaps in each rural county. Investments in T ech Innovation & Cybersecurity Enhancements for Rural NY Advances rural health care in New York by investing in innovative technologies and robust cybersecurity measures. This initiative deploys innovative digital health tools and platforms that streamline care delivery, enhance patient access, and support data-driven decision- making. The program focuses on fortifying the cybersecurity posture of rural health care facilities through advanced endpointprotection and comprehensive staff training. $212.06M Budget Period 1 Funding

North Carolina.initiatives_raw: North Carolina $216.82M Budget Period 2 Funding Initiative Name Initiative Description Build Rural Community Care Network “Hubs” Establishes locally governed networks called North Carolina Rural Organizations Orchestrating Transformation for Sustainability (NC ROOTS) Hubs to coordinate health services for rural residents. The hubs will connect people to medical, behavioral, and social supports, building on lessons learned from NC’s implementation of previous hub and spoke models. This initiative requires partnerships between the North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services (NCDHHS), healthcare providers, and community organizations. Create Models & Capacity for Expanded Primary Care, Prevention, and Chronic Disease Management Improves access to primary and preventive care for rural populations focused on chronic diseases and perinatal health. It expands successful programs like the 'I Gave Birth' model and coordinates with partners to manage conditions and improve nutrition. This effort will use NC ROOTS Hubs to connect families with community partners and fresh food resources in line with Food is Medicine efforts. Expand and Integrate Behavioral Health and Substance Use Disorder Services Expands access to mental health and substance use services in rural areas by building on the state's Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics (CCBHCs) model and coordinating efforts with regional ROOTS Hubs. This effort targets youth and adults by integrating care, launching mobile crisis teams, and using telehealth. Key partners include local health departments and community health centers implementing school-based services and various community organizations to improve care coordination. Build a Robust & Resilient Workforce & Innovative Care T eam Models for Rural Communities Strengthens the rural healthcare workforce by creating regional training hubs and expanding development programs. It focuses on training and retaining providers like social workers, doulas, and community health workers in rural communities. The initiative will partner with the NC ROOTS hubs, NC Community College System and universities to offer training and tuition support. Ensure Fiscal Sustainability of Rural Health Providers Through Innovative Financial Models Supports the financial health of rural hospitals and clinics by moving from payment models based on volume to ones based on value. It provides technical help and funding for providers to adopt these new models, building on NC Medicaid’s prior investment in population health and value- based payment. This will be done through the NC ROOTS Hubs with primary care providers and hospitals. $213.01M Budget Period 1 Funding
