Ohio.initiatives_raw: Ohio Initiative Name Initiative Description Ohio Rural School Based Health Centers (SBHCs) Improves healthcare access for children and the community by establishing sustainable clinics on school (K-12 and college) campuses. These centers provide primary care, dental care, screenings, behavioral health services, and telehealth connections with specialty providers, reducing student absenteeism and creating a pipeline for future clinicians at the college level. The initiative operates through partnerships with Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs), rural school districts, and the Ohio Department of Health (ODH). OH Student Eye Exam (SEE), vision, hearing, and dental services for rural students Expands mobile health services to provide vision, hearing, and dental care for students in rural areas. This program brings care directly to school campuses via mobile units, addressing the significant gap in follow-up care for students who fail initial screenings. It builds upon the existing OH SEE program by partnering with school districts and health providers, and universities across the state. Ohio Rural Health Innovation Hubs Establishes integrated networks of local providers to improve the quality, efficiency, and coordination of patient care in rural Ohio. These hubs support alliances among physicians, hospitals, and community resources to enhance patient outcomes while controlling costs. The initiative leverages partnerships with existing clinical networks and state agencies to help providers become self-sustaining. Rural Ohio Emergency Care Transformation Builds upon an existing pilot project to improve emergency response times and connect patients to the most appropriate level of care. This initiative scales alternate destination transport and treat-in-place options for rural communities across the state. It relies on partnerships between local EMS, hospitals, and other healthcare providers to reduce unnecessary emergency department visits. Rural Health Workforce Pipeline and Development Projects Develops a long-lasting pipeline of healthcare professionals by engaging students early and creating pathways to rural careers. The initiative coordinates activities between schools, colleges, and healthcare employers to provide work-based learning and career placement agreements. It supports these efforts by offering recruitment incentives and upskilling programs for community health workers and pharmacists. $202.03M Budget Period 1 Funding $201.93M Budget Period 2 Funding

Oklahoma.initiatives_raw: Oklahoma Initiative Name Initiative Description Innovating the Care Model Expands access to primary and specialty care for rural Oklahomans by deploying digital solutions, transportation support, andexpansion of the non-physician workforce. This initiative establishes a statewide telestroke network, expands RPM for maternal health, and integrates behavioral health into primary care settings. It leverages partnerships with the Oklahoma Association of Regional Councils (OARC) and the Oklahoma State Department of Health (OSDH) and enhances community paramedicine, doulas, and school-based health services. Moving Upstream Empowers individuals and communities to build a healthier Oklahoma through innovative, consumer-focused prevention programs. This initiative supports community-led wellness hubs, expands the use of community health workers (CHWs) in hospitals, and provides funding for chronic disease management. It leverages partnerships with local health departments to connect residents with community- based resources. Establishes a closed-loop community care platform, chronic disease management programs, consumer-facing technology for chronic disease prevention and management and behavioral health, lung cancer screening, and Presidential Fitness Test preparation funding. Facilitating Regional Collaboration Supports access to high-quality healthcare through strategic regionalization of services across the state. This initiative establishes a rural- focused Clinically Integrated Network (CIN) to foster collaboration and creates a centralized EMS platform to improve efficiency. It builds upon existing relationships between rural hospitals and the to gain scale through shared services. Develops a Rural Regional Reorientation Plan to bring rural hospitals and ecosystem partners (outpatient providers, long-term care, payers) together to align on the future system of care grounded in the needs of rural communities and oriented toward improved access to upstream prevention and primary care. Shifting to Value Builds a path to value-based care for primary care, behavioral health, and hospital providers. This initiative provides capacity-building funds for primary care practices to support value-based clinical extension models and expands the Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly (PACE). It supports providers serving dual-eligible populations by integrating Medicare and Medicaid financing to deliver comprehensive, team-based care. $223.48M Budget Period 1 Funding $227.10M Budget Period 2 Funding

Oregon.initiatives_raw: Oregon Initiative Name Initiative Description Regional Partnerships & System Transformation Applies regional solutions to enhance Oregon's shared healthcare infrastructure and promote financial stability in rural communities. This initiative funds local proposals to create and sustain partnerships between health care and social service entities. It leverages a hub-and- spoke model to improve care coordination and build long-term sustainability, with a focus on at-risk services like maternity care. Healthy Communities & Prevention Bolsters rural health systems by expanding access to integrated primary care and social health services that promote prevention and care management. The initiative supports Oregonians across all life stages, from expanding nurse home-visiting programs for new families to community-based services that help seniors age in place. It leverages local partnerships and technology-driven solutions to address health needs across the entire lifespan. Workforce Capacity & Resilience Addresses the growing shortage of health care professionals in rural communities through targeted investments and innovative strategies. This initiative expands Oregon’s skilled health care workforce by creating new training opportunities and long-term capacity across the state. It supports the current workforce by enhancing provider wellness and retention through peer support and expanded tele-mentoring. T echnology & Data Modernization Transforms Oregon's rural health communities through investments in enhanced technological approaches and solutions includingAI and remote patient monitoring. This initiative ensures digital access and secure sharing of health information, reducing administrative burden and improving coordination across providers, patients, and systems. It focuses on support for providers and rural communitiesto thoughtfully invest in technologies that meet their needs. Tribal Supports the Nine Federally Recognized Tribes of Oregon in implementing and enhancing projects that align with their individual priorities and goals. This initiative honors the self-determination and sovereignty of the Tribes, recognizing them as best positioned to lead healthcare transformation for their communities. It leverages partnerships between the Oregon Health Authority (OHA) and Tribal governments to ensure investments create long-lasting and sustainable impacts. $197.27M Budget Period 1 Funding $197.25M Budget Period 2 Funding

Pennsylvania.initiatives_raw: Pennsylvania Initiative Name Initiative Description* Maternal Health Creates regional rural Maternal Health Hubs to serve as centralized access points for comprehensive, coordinated maternity care. The initiative links hospitals, community providers, and behavioral health partners to ensure every pregnant and postpartum person has access to a full spectrum of services. It builds on existing partnerships with Rural Care Collaboratives (RCCs) to address regional needs and expand access to care. Behavioral Health Expands crisis services and increases access to care through remote behavioral health consultation and a telehealth bridge clinic for same-day Substance Use Disorder (SUD) treatment. The program expands the rural behavioral health workforce by offering educational awards for peer and recovery specialists and developing a statewide training management system. This initiative leverages partnerships with the PA Office of Vocational Rehabilitation and county agencies to support rural communities. Aging and Access Implements activities to reduce readmissions, build the nurse aide workforce, improve infection control, and simplify access to long-term care services statewide. The initiative funds targeted quality improvements in long-term care communities and expands the Program of All- Inclusive Care for the Elderly (PACE) to underserved rural counties. It leverages the state's "Aging Our Way, PA" strategic plan to support older adults and rural providers. EMS-Transportation Modernizes emergency medical services and infrastructure to improve readiness and response capacity in rural communities. This initiative strengthens the EMS workforce through targeted recruitment, training, and mental health mentorship programs. It leverages partnerships with regional EMS councils and county Public Safety Answering Points (PSAPs) to ensure resources are dispatched efficiently. $193.29M Budget Period 1 Funding $190.73M Budget Period 2 Funding

Rhode Island.initiatives_raw: Rhode Island Initiative Name Initiative Description Integrated Rural Population Health Infrastructure Establishes a comprehensive population health infrastructure by integrating clinical care hubs with community-led health networks. Transforms rural healthcare delivery by mobilizing local partners and resources to build healthier community environments. Delivers a strong clinical backbone that provides accessible, integrated medical care to rural residents. Rural Community- Integrated and Mobile Health Services Utilizes rural Community Learning Centers (CLCs) as multipurpose hubs for uses such as dedicated telemedicine spaces equippedwith advanced audiovisual technology, digital stethoscopes, and electrocardiogram machines. Deploys trained personnel to actively assist residents in accessing and navigating virtual medical visits encompassing disability services, lifestyle interventions, and pre- and post- natal support. Improves healthcare access for rural individuals by bridging the digital divide through hands-on technical support. Expanding Access to Rural Community Resources Addresses critical physical barriers that prevent older adults and persons with disabilities from accessing medical offices and community spaces. Funds the installation of equipment and other accessibility improvements in public facilities, as well as assessmentsand trainings to support these investments. Complements broader healthcare infrastructure efforts by making existing community resources physically accessible to all residents. Rural EMS Health Access and Integration Transforms EMS into an integrated, patient-centered extension of the traditional healthcare system scaling Rhode Island’s Mobile Integrated Health–Community Paramedicine (MIH-CP). Delivers preventive, urgent, and follow-up care directly within rural communities to improve patient outcomes. Reduces heavy reliance on emergency departments by resolving minor medical issues on-site. Rural Hospital-at-Home Program Strengthens local access to acute and post-acute services by establishing a scalable, home-based hospital care model. Delivers safe, high-quality medical treatment in patients' homes as a direct substitute for traditional inpatient admission. Replicates proven clinical standards to ensure safe and effective acute-level care outside of hospital walls while reducing costs. $156.17M Budget Period 1 Funding $158.17M Budget Period 2 Funding

policy_actions.text: Nutrition Continuing Medical Education Improved nutrition education among physicians through continuing medical education (CME) requirements can directly contribute to improving the health of Americans who live in rural areas given the disproportionate impact of chronic disease on rural America. This State Policy Action captures State efforts to require nutrition to be a component for CME. At baseline, RI did not require nutrition to be included in CME for physicians RI committed to this State Policy Action In Progress

Certificate of Need Certificate of Need (CON) laws require healthcare providers to seek permission from the State before they can open new facilities or expand service offerings. Eliminating or loosening CON laws allows providers to establish new facilities in underserved rural regions without increased burden, addressing the scarcity of local care options. This State Policy Action captures State efforts to ease CON laws across several service and facility types. At baseline, RI had stringent CON regulations RI committed to this State Policy Action Complete

Licensure Compacts Licensure compacts provide clinicians with the opportunity to serve patients across State borders, increasing the supply of accessible rural health providers. This State Policy Action captures State participation in licensure compacts for physicians, nursing, EMS, psychology, and Physician Assistants. At baseline, RI was a member of two of the five licensure compacts RI committed to this State Policy Action Complete: PA Compact

Scope of Practice Physician supply challenges in rural areas could be mitigated by expanding the scope of practice of other clinicians who have training and competency in caring for many of the cases currently limited to physician care. This State Policy Action captures State efforts to expand scope of practice for Physician Assistants, Nurse Practitioners, Pharmacists, and Dental Hygienists. At baseline, RI had moderate scope of practice (SOP) for PAs, full SOP for NPs, restricted SOP for Pharmacists, and semi-restricted SOP for Dental Hygienists RI committed to this State Policy Action No Progress: Pharmacist SOP Complete: Dental Hygienist SOP

South Carolina.initiatives_raw: South Carolina Initiative Name Initiative Description Connections to Care Expands digital infrastructure by implementing electronic health records, remote patient monitoring, telehealth services and a statewide resource database platform to improve care coordination and access. Assists health care entities in transitions from a paper-based system to a fully electronic medical record system with integrated modules, to improve interoperability, reduce duplication, and support value-based care, as well as to improve care coordination and streamline admissions. Implements a patient-facing digital intake platform in rural clinics to streamline documentation and identify drivers of health outcomes at the point of care. Supports purchasing standards- based (to promote interoperability) remote patient monitoring (RPM) equipment for diabetes, hypertension, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and heart disease patients, and the monitoring infrastructure for providers, with staff support formonitoring and troubleshooting. Leveling Up Scales successful pilot programs statewide, focusing on chronic disease management, pediatric care quality, and workforce development. This initiative expands proven local and regional programs, such as care coordination models and school mental health programs, to reach all rural communities. The program enhances Graduate Medical Education (GME) by partnering with rural hospitals to improve training experiences, scales proven chronic disease programs and successful pilot programs, and conducts comprehensive needs assessments to identify gaps in access, infrastructure, and services, ensuring future investments are data-driven and sustainable. Wellness Within Reach Deploys mobile health units, crisis response teams, and pop-up clinics to bring care directly to underserved populations. Supports mobile crisis response improvements, expands community care sites including permanent clinics, seasonal pop-ups, mobile vans, and intermittent service locations, emergency medical services. Establishes community-based health kiosks with equipment and supplies for a 24-hour pharmacy kiosk that distributes necessary medications in rural healthcare locations. $200.03M Budget Period 1 Funding $195.99M Budget Period 2 Funding

South Dakota.initiatives_raw: South Dakota Initiative Name Initiative Description T ech and Data Connection for a Healthier South Dakota Modernizes healthcare delivery through a comprehensive approach to digital health infrastructure and information exchange. This initiative provides funding to help healthcare facilities adopt electronic health records (EHRs) and unifies siloed data into a single platform. It leverages the South Dakota Health Data Atlas to enable providers and policymakers to make better data-driven decisions. Building a Sustainable Rural Healthcare Workforce Strengthens the state's rural health workforce by offering tiered sign-on bonuses and relocation assistance to attract new professionals. This initiative supports the existing workforce with funding for education and certification to improve retention in high-need rural areas. The program relies on partnerships with technical colleges and universities to create a stable and skilled workforce. Expand and Strengthen Rural Community Health Worker (CHW) Workforce Establishes a robust community health worker (CHW) and community health representative (CHR) workforce to serve as a bridge between clinical care and community services. The initiative develops a CHW/CHR training and certification program and provides financial support to rural healthcare providers to hire and deploy CHWs. It partners with the South Dakota Department of Health and local health systems to improve care coordination for underserved populations. Rural Health Forward: Training and Resource Hub Creates a centralized hub to deliver best-in-class training, technical assistance, and leadership development for rural healthcare providers and allied health workers. The initiative helps rural facilities adapt to new care delivery models and improve financial stability. This program leverages partnerships with state universities, medical schools, and long-term care and home health agencies to ensure providershave the tools to succeed. Medicaid Primary Accountable Care Transformation Improves health outcomes and lowers costs by moving primary care practices from a fee-for-service model to a value-based payment system. This initiative offers flexible, capitated payments that give providers the resources and autonomy to deliver patient-centered care. The program will leverage South Dakota Medicaid's managed care program to incentivize quality outcomes over volume. $189.48M Budget Period 1 Funding $187.65M Budget Period 2 Funding

Tennessee.initiatives_raw: Tennessee Initiative Name Initiative Description Healthcare Resiliency Program: Service Line Expansion & Co-Location Utilizes the proven Healthcare Resiliency Program (HRP) model to improve health outcomes. Expands access to comprehensive healthcare for rural communities through a competitive grant process. This initiative helps rural hospitals and clinics add or expand needed services like perinatal care, behavioral health, and primary care. Last Mile T eams Unifies multiple efforts to expand emergency care and bring integrated health services to hard-to-reach areas. It builds upon existing programs like Project Rural Recovery and the Community Health Access and Navigation in T ennessee (CHANT) program to connect pregnant and post-partum women with critical care. Texas.initiatives_raw: Texas Initiative Name Initiative Description Make Rural T exans Healthy Again Part 1 issues targeted direct awards to Rural Hospital Districts and authorities with a publicly owned and operated hospital within their jurisdiction. Part 2 issued target grants through a competitive process to public and private rural hospitals to enhance community-based prevention, wellness, and nutrition programs. Targets the reduction of critical chronic conditions including diabetes, cardiovascular disease, chronic respiratory illness, and obesity among rural residents. Promotes healthier lifestyles through localized education and wellness services to improve long-term medical outcomes. Rural Texas Patients in the Driver's Seat Invests in technology to establish consumer-facing health portals that engage patients and facilitate the exchange of health information between patients, providers, and payers. Empowers rural residents to communicate directly with their healthcare teams throughsecure messaging and virtual visits. Provides providers and payers with access to patient medical documentation and health information to make informed care and coverage decisions. Lone Star Advanced AI and T elehealth Invest in AI and telehealth technologies to assist rural health care providers in their work to predict and improve patience outcomes, maintain care and more efficiently adjust medication and therapy for patience and linking rural primary care providers and their patients directly to specialized clinical experts. Funding also includes establishing local, patient-focused hubs where they can receive telehealth care. The Next Generation of the Small T own Doctor and T eam Strengthens the rural healthcare workforce by surrounding local physicians with midlevel practitioners and allied health professionals. Delivers comprehensive, community-based medical care to rural residents by expanding local clinical teams. Reduces regional shortages of essential health professionals by implementing targeted recruitment for specific provider types and retention for providers. Locally driven efforts will focus on developing career paths for local high school students, providing educational awards for recent high school graduates, offering relocation or signing bonuses for early, mid, or late career professionals, creating a new residency training program, fellowship or combination program, including partnering with academic institutions or an existing teaching hospital. $281.32M Budget Period 1 Funding $281.98M Budget Period 2 Funding

Utah.initiatives_raw: Utah Initiative Name Initiative Description Making Rural Utahns Healthy: Preventive Action and Transformation for Health (PATH) Advances rural health through innovations in nutrition, physical activity, and built environments to establish lifelong healthy behaviors and impact maternal and behavioral health. Establishes community care hubs using regional stakeholder groups to create integratedmodels that improve physical and mental health and funding local partners to support efforts including nutritious foods and physicalactivity. Targets rural Utahns across their entire lifespan to prevent chronic disease and support behavioral health. Rural Incentive and Skill Expansion (RISE) Invests in career pathways starting in grade school to build a sustainable rural healthcare workforce. Connects local education and expanded clinical training directly to regional healthcare needs and expands on the capacity of rural clinical preceptor programs across various provider types. Aligns with state leadership goals to increase the total number of primary care providers in rural counties by five percent. Sustaining Health Infrastructure for Transformation (SHIFT) Transforms preventive care through targeted enhancements to local service delivery including the introduction of a 24/7 crisis stabilization center and multi-purpose facilities delivering preventive and specialist care services. Builds a resilient, interconnected system centered on proactive wellness, early clinical intervention, and care delivered at home. Addresses interconnected economic, infrastructure, and workforce barriers that cause disproportionately poor health outcomes in rural populations. Financial Approaches for Sustainable Transformation (FAST) Resolves core financial and care delivery challenges that hinder the viability of rural healthcare in Utah. Transitions localproviders to value- based payment models and proactive care while streamlining revenue cycles for efficiency. Pilots alternative funding models to secure reliable specialist access for rural communities and allow patients to receive care from home. Leveraging Innovation for Facilitated T elehealth (LIFT) Improves physical and behavioral healthcare access in rural communities through scalable, data-informed telehealth strategies. Delivers hands-on training and technical assistance to facilitate effective technology implementation and lasting impact. Expands timely access to high-quality care to address lower cancer survival rates and higher rates of suicide. $195.74M Budget Period 1 Funding $191.92M Budget Period 2 Funding

Vermont.initiatives_raw: Vermont Initiative Name Initiative Description Regionalization and Innovative Care Strategies Conducts detailed strategic planning and implementation to establish a transformed, regional system of care ensuring health services are right sized and optimally distributed. Expands immediate access to community-based care through new urgent care and mobile medical units. Invests in specialized equipment like dialysis units and ventilators to deliver high-acuity services to nursing home residents. Establishing a Clinically Integrated Network of Shared Services Fosters collaboration and partnerships across the continuum of healthcare providers in the state collaborating with an organizing entity to implement initiative components. Implements a system of shared services to produce operational efficiencies, lower costs, andpreserve patient choice. Funds the purchase of necessary clinical technologies, including telehealth, electronic consultations, remotepatient monitoring, and artificial intelligence scribes. Strengthening Primary Care Creates a modern, enhanced iteration of the state's existing Blueprint model to upgrade the current model originating in 2005. Focuses on integrated treatment for complex chronic conditions, evidence-based workforce training, and analytical and technical practice transformation assistance. Delivers continuous quality improvements to establish a highly coordinated learning and performance monitoring network. Health Care Workforce Development Strengthens the state's rural healthcare pipeline through strategic investments in recruitment, training, and retention. Enables local clinical providers to operate at the top of their professional licenses. Fosters a sustainable network of skilled professionals to improve overall care delivery in underserved areas and encourages partnerships among hospitals, educational institutions, and community partners. Price Transparency and Insurance Competition Increases access to affordable, high-quality care for rural residents by improving pricing transparency and insurance market participation. Enhances the state's ability to analyze cost, quality, and access metrics through a new technical platform accessible to policymakers, regulators, and the public. Supports a statewide assessment to evaluate options for expanding affordable health coverage options. $195.05M Budget Period 1 Funding $190.00M Budget Period 2 Funding

Virginia.initiatives_raw: Virginia Initiative Name Initiative Description CareIQ Advances innovative technologies that promote efficient care delivery, improved provider satisfaction, and enhanced patient outcomes in rural areas. Enables local healthcare providers to leapfrog outdated service models to deliver highly effective, data-informed medical treatments. Supports clinical decision-making through the deployment of modern digital health tools. Supports early-stage health technology start-ups based in Virginia, providers in adoption new, pre-selected tools to improve productivity through better decision support, documentation automation, workflow efficiency, and adopting upgraded EHR, cybersecurity and data analytics platforms, and hospitals to support scaling of remote patient monitoring (RPM). Homegrown Health Heroes Grows the rural provider workforce while providing clear career pipelines and economic opportunities for rural Virginians. Builds a sustainable local talent pipeline to address critical medical staffing shortages in underserved communities. Encourages residents to train and remain in their home counties as highly skilled clinical professionals. Funds residency slots across rural health systemsin priority specialties, supports stand up of mobile labs, and expands capacity for existing and new healthcare credentials. Connected Care, Closer to Home Rewires how rural healthcare is delivered by bringing essential services directly into remote communities. Expands local access to primary, urgent, specialty, substance use disorder, dental, vision, and maternity care. Supports mobile care units, telehealth kiosks, “clinics in a box” , e consults, and development of “hubs” . Supports local EMS in training, staffing, and equipping to expand scope of services. Supports innovative maternal care through technical assistance for RPM. Live Well, Together Focuses on preventing chronic disease through a series of community-based, whole-health sub-initiatives. Supports Food as Medicine sub-initiative by piloting food pharmacies that offer produce, nutrition counseling, and medically tailored meals for food insecure patients with or at risk of chronic disease or recently discharged from the hospital. Pilots integrated chronic disease management programs to scale approaches to monitor and support high needs patients. Supports minor renovation and repurposing of community spaces into recreational spaces for structured physical activity programs, sports, and wellness education. Provides community-based education and engagement to support dual-eligible seniors in navigation of health care coverage and enrollment in integrated care plans. Virginia is also implementing a Rural Technology Catalyst Fund, which promotes consumer-facing, technology-driven solutions for chronic disease prevention and management in rural populations. $189.54M Budget Period 1 Funding $195.71M Budget Period 2 Funding

Washington.initiatives_raw: Washington Initiative Name Initiative Description Ignite innovation in Washington’s rural hospitals Strengthens the financial health and sustainability of The Rural Collaborative (TRC), 30 independent rural hospitals, throughnew business models, technology, and forms of cooperation. This initiative expands a rural health network to create greater efficiencies and broadens the pathway for hospitals to participate in value-based care arrangements, shared staffing, and group purchasing. It leverages partnerships with the TRC and the Washington State Hospital Association (WSHA) to improve hospital operating efficiency. Prevent disease and manage care in community settings Builds and expands programs that support rural residents in settings outside the walls of clinical systems. The initiative expands the community-based workforce, develops dementia-capable communities, and modernizes emergency medical services transport to reduce delays for time-sensitive emergencies. It leverages partnerships with existing community hubs like senior centers, churches, and schools to promote prevention and connect people to social services. Invest in the health of Native families Improves the health and well-being of Native families by making critical investments in workforce development and care coordination. This initiative supports the training and hiring of Community Health Representatives, doulas , and other community-based workersto help families navigate complex health systems. It fosters strategic partnerships between Tribes and local hospitals through written care coordination agreements. Adopt technology and data solutions to enable health improvements Provides start-up funding and technical assistance for new and emerging technologies that increase efficiency, access, and quality in Washington's rural health care system. This initiative expands remote care services and provider mentorship through Project ECHO (Extension for Community Healthcare Outcomes) and invests in a provider technology fund for tools like AI, remote patient monitoring, and telehealth. It leverages partnerships with the University of Washington and other medical centers to bring expertise to rural communities. $181.26M Budget Period 1 Funding $177.06M Budget Period 2 Funding

West Virginia.initiatives_raw: West Virginia Initiative Name Initiative Description Connected Care Grid Builds the infrastructure to bring virtual and in-person primary, preventive, urgent, and specialist care access to people on-demand. This initiative bridges the gap between urban and rural communities by creating an integrated network that connects clinics, homes, and hospitals through modern technology. It expands specialty care access by leveraging partnerships with the WV Health Information Network (WVHIN) and local provider hubs. Rural Health Link Addresses transportation barriers by enabling access to a unified health-mobility platform for rural residents. The initiative connects citizens to transport options like public buses, rideshares, and volunteers for non-emergency medical needs. It builds on existing Medicaid non-emergency medical transportation (NEMT) and regional transit programs by partnering with the Departments of Health and Transportation to reduce missed appointments. Mountain State Care Force Addresses persistent health workforce shortages by developing home-grown talent and attracting providers to the state. This initiative expands rural residency programs and offers incentives for providers who commit to practicing in rural areas. It builds on existing state workforce programs by partnering with West Virginia's medical schools, the community and technical college system, and K-12 education. Smart Care Catalyst Helps rural providers reduce administrative burden and modernize operations by focusing on value and quality. This initiativesupports the transition from fee-for-service to outcomes-driven payment models that improve both the quality and affordability of healthcare.It will partner with managed care organizations and commercial payers to develop standardized, multi-payer value-based care models. Health to Prosperity Tackles health issues that pose barriers to employment by connecting adults with chronic conditions to coordinated care and job placement. The initiative helps employees stay healthy by embedding wellness and preventive services directly in the workplace. It expands on successful state programs by partnering with employers and Medicaid managed care organizations (MCOs). $199.48M Budget Period 1 Funding $202.08M Budget Period 2 Funding

Wyoming.initiatives_raw: Wyoming Initiative Name Initiative Description Access to emergency medical care Shores up rural Wyoming's access to basic medical infrastructure across underserved communities. Secures essential regional resources for ambulance services, emergency departments, and labor and delivery units. Establishes the “Critical Access Hospital – Basic” (CAHB) incentive program to offer essential community services and emergency medical services regionalization efforts. Rural workforce supply Grows the supply of essential healthcare workers across Wyoming using a strategic combination of individual education supportawards, educational capacity grants, and the 5-year required service periods. Expands training capacity at local schools while implementing mandatory five-year service commitments in rural areas. Establishes a highly skilled, sustainable workforce to meet the long-term clinical needs of remote counties through workforce education individual support, physician post-graduate medical education slots, workforce education start-up. Health technology transformation Leverages sensible technology investments to help groups of rural providers deliver better patient care closer to home. Expands remote patient access to clinical consultations and deepens the patient-provider relationship through virtual communication tools. Enhances the long-term management of chronic diseases while improving clinical efficiency through regional collaboration. Addresses the technology adoption challenge to improve care delivery closer to home, build interoperability across providers, and cut wasteful administrative activity. Establishes a statewide tele-specialist platform, a non-emergency transportation coordination platform, and improved centralized billing capacity. Make Wyoming Healthy Again Improves the metabolic, behavioral, and cardiovascular health of rural residents through integrated primary care expansion, clinically- integrated care coordination for chronic disease, exercise, and healthy diet promotion. Integrated primary care expansion increases the number and geographical reach of Federally Qualified Health Centers around Wyoming, with a focus on improving the integrationof primary care with behavioral health, obstetric and gynecological care, as well as dental and preventive health services. Exercise and healthy diet promotion efforts establish partnerships with local non-profits to defray operational costs for organizing physicalevidence- based activities. $205.00M Budget Period 1 Funding $207.23M Budget Period 2 Funding
